html:
The Wergaia are an Aboriginal people of northwest Victoria, in the Mallee and Wimmera regions, around Lake Hindmarsh, Lake Albacutya and the Wimmera River. They were also known as Maligundidj, the people of the mallee scrub that covers much of their country.

Their neighbours included the Jardwadjali and Wotjobaluk to the south, the Wemba Wemba to the east and the Latje Latje to the north. Their lakes fill only in wet years, and people moved with the water.

Squatters reached the Wimmera in the 1840s. In 1859 Moravian missionaries founded the Ebenezer Mission at Lake Hindmarsh, where many Wergaia people lived until it closed in 1904. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
